inclusion.I2: Human participants performing an emotion regulation or reappraisal task, broadly defined. Reappraisal covers a wide spectrum of tactics including reinterpretation, perspective-taking, and distancing.
inclusion.I3: Includes at least one group of healthy adults. A study of a patient population qualifies if it also includes a healthy control group.

exclusion.E1: Non-empirical papers (e.g., reviews, meta-analyses) without original human data.
exclusion.E2: Doesn't include at least one healthy adult sample.
exclusion.E3: Empathy or perspective-taking studies in which participants adopt a self-oriented or other-oriented perspective toward a depicted person WITHOUT being instructed to amplify or attenuate their own emotional response. These belong to the empathy arm of the literature, not the emotion regulation arm. If the abstract indicates an explicit regulation goal (increase/decrease/maintain one's own emotion), include it.

inclusion.I6: fMRI Task- reappraisal used as the emotion regulation strategy, construed broadly to include reinterpretation, perspective-taking, and distancing tactics. The regulation goal may be up-regulation (increase) OR down-regulation (decrease) of emotion, and the emotional stimuli may be positive OR negative. A study qualifies if it implements EITHER regulation direction with EITHER stimulus valence; it does NOT need to include both directions or both valences.
inclusion.I7: Stimuli- the emotional stimuli being regulated are static visual images (e.g., IAPS pictures, photographs of faces or scenes). Exclude studies in which the regulated stimuli are film or video clips, audio, narrative scripts, imagined or recalled autobiographical scenarios, monetary or social decision outcomes, anticipatory cues, or delivered pain/shock.
inclusion.I8: Target sample- at least one group of healthy adults with no prior report of neurological, medical, or psychiatric disorders. A study of a patient or clinical population qualifies only if results for the healthy control group are reported separately; only that group is of interest.
inclusion.I9: Analysis- Reports at least one within-task contrast related to emotion regulation (e.g., “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”, “up-regulate > maintain”) for the target sample.
inclusion.I10: Whole-brain evidence- The target analysis must be a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map, with peak coordinates reported in a standard anatomical reference space (Talairach/Tournoux or MNI).
inclusion.I11: It is acceptable for qualifying whole-brain results to be reported in tables of coordinates, figures, or supplementary materials, as long as they are clearly described in the text.

exclusion.E4: Non-empirical papers (e.g., reviews, meta-analyses, methods-only, simulations) without original fMRI data in healthy adults.
exclusion.E5: Studies that report only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses, only small-volume corrected results, or that used partial brain coverage, without an accompanying whole-brain map.
exclusion.E6: Studies that report only seed-based connectivity, effective connectivity (e.g., PPI, DCM), or resting-state analyses (e.g., ICA, PLE, Hurst exponents) without also reporting a whole-brain task activation map.
exclusion.E7: Studies that report only between-group contrasts or interactions (e.g., subgroup vs subgroup, patient vs control, gender differences)
exclusion.E8: Empathy or perspective-taking studies in which participants take a self-oriented or other-oriented perspective toward a depicted person with no instruction to amplify or attenuate their own emotional response. A perspective-taking or distancing manipulation WITH an explicit regulation goal is reappraisal and qualifies.

inclusion.GLOBAL_I1: Voxelwise task evidence- this analysis must itself be a group-level, univariate, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map. A study qualifying on the strength of one whole-brain analysis does not make its other analyses eligible.
inclusion.GLOBAL_I2: The contrast must be WITHIN-group, and must concern either the regulation of an emotional response or the passive unregulated viewing of emotional stimuli.
inclusion.GLOBAL_I3: Direction- either an ACTIVATION or a DEACTIVATION effect qualifies.
inclusion.GLOBAL_I4: Judge this analysis from its own name, description and table caption. An empty or generic analysis name (e.g. "analysis_0") is never itself a reason to exclude- it usually means the analysis is the only one in its table, so the caption describes it fully.
inclusion.GLOBAL_I5: Assign every label that applies. A regulation contrast carries TWO labels: its goal (decrease or increase) and the strategy label (reappraisal).

exclusion.GLOBAL_E1: This analysis is a region-of-interest (ROI) or small-volume-corrected result rather than a voxelwise whole-brain map.
exclusion.GLOBAL_E2: This analysis is a connectivity or resting-state result- seed-based or effective connectivity, PPI, DCM, ICA- rather than a task activation map.
exclusion.GLOBAL_E3: This contrast is between two participant GROUPS, or a group x condition interaction, including gender and other subgroup difference effects.
exclusion.GLOBAL_E4: This contrast isolates an emotion regulation strategy that the study frames as distinct from reappraisal- e.g. expressive suppression, or attentional distraction run as its own condition. Reinterpretation, perspective-taking and distancing are tactics WITHIN reappraisal and do qualify.

inclusion.REAPPRAISAL_I1: The contrast isolates a reappraisal regulation attempt against a less-regulated or unregulated comparison- typical forms are reappraise > look, reappraise > view, reappraise > watch, reappraise > maintain, decrease > look, or increase > maintain.
inclusion.REAPPRAISAL_I2: Either regulation goal qualifies, since this label is the union of decrease and increase. Assign it IN ADDITION to the goal label, never instead of it.

exclusion.REAPPRAISAL_E1: Passive viewing contrasts with no regulation instruction.

inclusion.DECREASE_I1: The contrast's regulation goal is to reduce or dampen the emotional response- e.g. decrease > look, decrease > maintain, downregulate > view, "distance oneself".

exclusion.DECREASE_E1: Contrasts whose ONLY stated goal is to amplify emotion.

inclusion.INCREASE_I1: The contrast's regulation goal is explicitly to amplify or intensify the emotional response- e.g. increase > maintain, increase > look, increase > view, upregulate > watch, "feel the emotion more intensely".
inclusion.INCREASE_I2: Up-regulation must be stated or clearly implied by the condition name.
inclusion.INCREASE_I3: A contrast that POOLS both regulation directions does qualify, in addition to decrease. The signature is a generic regulation contrast ("regulate > view", "task > emotion") in a study whose design had both an up- and a down-regulation condition.

exclusion.INCREASE_E1: Contrasts whose only stated goal is to dampen emotion.

inclusion.MAINTAIN_I1: The contrast reflects passive, uninstructed viewing of emotional stimuli- e.g. emotion > baseline, look negative > baseline, view emotional > neutral, watch > rest. The defining feature is the ABSENCE of any regulation instruction.

exclusion.MAINTAIN_E1: Any contrast involving a regulation attempt. `maintain` is mutually exclusive with the other three labels- if the participant was told to change their emotional response, it is not maintain.
